Theme

Town, shops & places

Belgrade noun

Renaissance

M-O s.v. Belgrade (Tursellinus 1652)

Belgradum, Belgradī n.

noun, second declension

A town takes no preposition: Belgradum (to), Belgradī (in, at), Belgradō (from).

Other words

  • Singidūnum, Singidūnī n.

    noun, second declension · also used · late Latin · Sulp. Sev. Chron. 2.38.3: ā Singidūnō Ursatius; Not. Dign. Or. 41: Singidūnō; M-O s.v. Belgrade; Graesse, Orbis Latinus (1861), index s.v. Belgrad: Singidunum, Taurunum

    The ancient name, in late writers (Sulpicius Severus, the Notitia dignitatum); Lewis & Short has no entry for it. The long ū is Morgan–Owens’s marking.

See also Serbia, Danube.

SourcesMorgan–Owens, Adumbratio, geographical section, with the authorities it cites (cited as M-O s.v.).

J. G. Th. Graesse, Orbis Latinus (Dresden, 1861), German–Latin index, read in the scan at archive.org (the 1909 edition at columbia.edu could not be reached page by page); its forms are post-classical unless Lewis & Short has them.

The Latin Library texts (thelatinlibrary.com), read in a local copy, for ancient passages not quoted in Lewis & Short; cited by book and section.
